question: What is the main reason a nurse performs an eye irrigation?

options.A: To flush out chemicals or foreign bodies from the eye
options.B: To deliver antibiotic eye drops for a bacterial infection
options.C: To permanently dilate the pupil for a detailed eye exam
options.D: To measure the exact intraocular pressure of the globe

explanation: Great job thinking practically! Irrigation uses a steady stream of fluid to wash away dangerous substances or particles before they hurt the eye tissues. You've got this!

question: Why do you need to act immediately when a patient gets a chemical splash in the eye?

options.A: Chemicals quickly burn and damage delicate eye tissues
options.B: Waiting prevents the nurse from finding a neutralizing agent
options.C: Delayed washing allows the chemical to crystallize into a solid
options.D: Chemical splashes rapidly lower the normal body temperature

explanation: Time is precious here! Harsh substances start destroying eye cells right away, so washing them out fast stops permanent injury.

question: When should you NEVER perform routine eye irrigation?

options.A: Mild redness caused by ordinary environmental dust
options.B: A suspected penetrating injury or rupture of the eyeball
options.C: A chemical splash involving standard household bleach
options.D: A small speck of sand trapped under the lower eyelid

explanation: Remember: if the eyeball itself is cut open or ruptured, pushing fluid in will raise pressure and push the inside out. Always check for a puncture first!

question: A patient comes in with a metal flake stuck on the surface of their eye. Why is irrigation a good choice here?

options.A: Fluid pressure forces the metal deeper to hide the pain
options.B: Washing the eye replaces the need for a physical eye exam
options.C: Irrigation completely dissolves metal on contact
options.D: The fluid stream can safely flush away loose surface irritants

explanation: Spot on! If something is just resting loosely on the surface, a gentle, steady flow of liquid is a safe way to float it right out.

question: Which fluid solution is preferred for a standard eye wash?
explanation: Normal saline is isotonic, meaning it matches the natural fluid balance of the eye so it won't harm delicate cells while cleaning.

question: Why should you avoid using plain distilled water for an eye wash?

options.A: Plain water freezes too quickly when exposed to room air
options.B: Isotonic solutions have a bright color to track the runoff
options.C: Distilled water instantly burns the skin around the eye
options.D: Distilled water causes fluid to move into cells and swell them

explanation: Plain water lacks salt balance (it's hypotonic), so it crosses into eye cells and causes them to swell and damage. Stick to saline!

question: How should you position your patient's head during an eye wash?

options.A: Tilted slightly toward the affected side
options.B: Tilted firmly toward the unaffected side
options.C: Positioned flat and facing straight up
options.D: Tilted backward as far as the neck allows

explanation: Tilting toward the bad side ensures the dirty runoff flows away off the face instead of spilling into the healthy eye.

question: Why does a nurse test tear pH with paper before treating a chemical splash?

options.A: To determine if the patient needs local numbing eye drops first
options.B: To prove that the patient is experiencing a severe allergic reaction
options.C: To measure how severe the chemical exposure is and guide treatment
options.D: To check if the patient has a hidden bacterial eye infection

explanation: Checking the pH tells you if it was an acid or an alkali burn, and you keep washing until the pH goes back to normal. Smart nursing!

question: When starting an eye irrigation, where do you aim the stream of fluid?

options.A: Directly onto the center of the black pupil
options.B: At the outer corner, flowing inward toward the nose
options.C: Directly against the upper eyelid skin
options.D: At the inner canthus, flowing toward the outer canthus

explanation: Always flow from the inside corner (near the nose) toward the outside corner. This follows natural tear flow and keeps junk out of the tear ducts!

question: A student nurse is getting ready to irrigate an eye. Which action means they need a quick correction?

options.A: Placing a waterproof towel and a kidney basin under the cheek
options.B: Encouraging the patient to blink periodically during the wash
options.C: Resting fingers directly upon the patient's eyeball to hold it open
options.D: Holding the irrigation tubing about one inch away from the eye

explanation: Ouch! Always rest your fingers on the bony cheekbone or forehead, never directly on the eyeball, to prevent accidental pressure injury.

question: What is an important final step after finishing an eye irrigation for a chemical burn?

options.A: Rechecking the tear pH to ensure it has returned to normal
options.B: Rinsing the patient's entire face with rubbing alcohol
options.C: Instructing the patient to avoid blinking for two hours
options.D: Applying a tight eye patch with heavy pressure tape

explanation: Checking the pH one last time confirms that all the harmful chemical has been fully neutralized and washed away. Great wrap-up!

question: Why is charting the details of an eye irrigation so important in the patient's record?

options.A: It proves to the pharmacy department that sterile supplies were wasted
options.B: It provides a clear legal record of solution amount, duration, and patient response
options.C: It prevents the patient from receiving any further medical bills
options.D: It guarantees that the patient will regain full vision by tomorrow

explanation: Good documentation protects both you and the patient by proving exactly what care was given and how the patient responded.

question: Which of these is a common complication if an eye irrigation is done carelessly?

options.A: Corneal abrasion from equipment or trapped debris
options.C: Total loss of the patient's sense of smell
options.D: Sudden fracture of the orbital cheekbone

explanation: Rough handling or dragging particles across the eye can scratch the delicate cornea. Always be gentle!

question: What should you do right away if a patient says their eye pain and blurriness are getting worse during an irrigation?

options.A: Stop the irrigation and notify the healthcare provider
options.B: Turn off the room lights and leave the patient alone to rest
options.C: Increase the fluid flow rate to wash the pain away faster
options.D: Ignore the complaint because pain is normal during a flush

explanation: Never ignore worsening pain! Stop right away and let the doctor know so they can check for further injury or complications.
